tools.name: wake_check_site
tools.description: Probe a public hostname the way an AI agent sees it (homepage, robots.txt, llms.txt, sitemap, agent card) and return scores out of 100 with concrete recommendations and publish-ready llms.txt / robots files. Input is a hostname only; the probe keeps structural signals, never page bodies. No account

tools.name: wake_signup
tools.description: Create the account and the desk for a website you own and get an API key back, so you can install the tracker and read the desk over MCP. Needs site, email and terms_accepted: true (terms: /wake/docs/terms.md, privacy: /wake/docs/privacy.md). One desk per host; rate-limited.

tools.name: wake_about
tools.description: One paragraph on Wake (agent experience optimization and agent engine optimization for a website), with links to docs, API, MCP and signup.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: wake_signup · Private data: wake_check_site, wake_signup · Public sink: wake_check_site, wake_signup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: wake_signup · Private data: wake_check_site, wake_signup · Public sink: wake_check_site, wake_signup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
